This petition is filed by the injured petitioner U/s.22 of Employee's Compensation Act claiming compensation from the respondents for the injuries sustained by him during the course of his employment on 16-02-2022.
2.
It is the case of the petitioner that: The petitioner is a workman employed in the respondent Factory since several years.

In the course of his work, on 16-02-2022 in the first shift 6-00 am., to Kiran K R vs Fedaral Mogul Goetze India Ltd on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115107610/
1 2.00 pm., he received instruction from his supervisor Narasimha Murthy, to carry out the work of charging the main furnace by placing the pouring Ladle to Burner-1 for pre- heating in order to start pouring.

sentences.text: At that time he observed that the treatment ladle was already placed for pre- heating at Burner-1 by his co-workers Prabhulinga and M Sriram.
Further he observed that the treatment ladle heating had been completed and the burner was in AUTOOFF condition.

At that time no other workers or fork lift was available in pre-heating area, as fork lift operator Prabhulinga and one more co-worker Sriram were engaged in the work of stocking charging materials next to the furnace.

The petitioner got instructions from supervisor to place the pouring Ladle for preheating to start pouring through fixed term employee, he attempted to pull the trolley backside manually on which 350 kg treatment Ladle was placed for preheating at Burner-1.
In this process when he pulled the trolley backside by about 2 to 4 meters from burner point, due to unevenness of the flooring his right foot and the trolley wheels got stuck and jammed together.
The trolley along with 350 kg treatment Ladle toppled and fell on his right foot, causing serious crush injury to his ankle.
3. The petitioner was helped by his co-workmen they shifted him to the Health Centre in the factory premises.
After administering first aid he was shifted to M/s Manipal Hospital, Hebbal wherein multiple surgeries were conducted to treat the injury.
Thereafter the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient at Manipal Hospital from 16-02-2022 to 21-02-2022 wherein implants were fixed.
Again the petitioner was admitted in the said hospital from 03-01-2024 to 06-01-2024 wherein surgery was conducted in the pelvic region and bones was removed from that area is inserted to the ankle.
4. Due to the permanent disability, the petitioner cannot stand for long hours and also unable to walk continuously for more than 10 to 15 minutes.
He is dependent on the walking stick without which he cannot walk.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy.
He was getting a monthly salary of Rs.50,000/- and he is not covered under the E.S.I.
The case was registered against the respondent by the Deputy Director of Factories, Division -3 in CC No.15175/2022 for the offence punishable u/Sec. 92 of Factories Act.
Hence, the respondent is liable to pay compensation as per the Employee's Compensation Act.
5. The respondent has filed written statement and contended that their company has modern production facilities in India including in Bengaluru, which has been in production for 43 years.
He has put in place a system under which implementation of labour laws is monitored and it is ensured that there is no deviation of any nature particularly with regard to health and safety.

6. All the workers including the injured worker were specifically trained with respect to safety aspects that needs to be followed in the shop floor from time to time in all the manufacturing process including ladle Pre- heating.
An 'On job training report' along with feedback/reaction sheet was generated after the training.
7. The respondent further contended that they conducts safety month every year in order to enhance safety awareness among the employees.
During this employees are given the opportunity to share their experiences and many safely competitions are conducted and also appointed two Safety Officers who are qualified in industrial safely.
They go around the factory and ensure that the employees adopt the safety measures as specified by them and mentioned in the Safety Policy.

sentences.text: The respondent has admitted that, petitioner is a regular employee who is in the service of the respondent w.e.f 05-08-2009.

The petitioner was on duty in the Ring Foundry on 16-02-2022 in a shift (06.00 am., to 02.00 pm.,).
9.

The respondent further contended that at about 8-00 am., the petitioner of his own accord and without informing his supervisor pulled the trolley with KVI Metal treatment ladle backwards around 2 meters before taking a turn towards his right hand side, due to which the trolley went out of balance and toppled and that the toppled ladle and trolley fell on the employee's right ankle resulting in crush injury.

10. The respondent further contended that the injured worker was immediately shifted to the Occupational Health Centre of the factory wherein first aid treatment was given and then the petitioner was shifted to Manipal Hospitals for further treatment.

The Orthopaedic doctor described the injury as crush injury with multiple fracture (lower end of both bones tibia and fibula fracture)
and underwent surgery.
The doctors were of the view that as per the petitioner's condition, there is less likelihood of suffering any disability and he will be able to take normal duties after rest and treatment.

11. The respondent further contended that the trolley was made for the purpose of keeping the treatment ladle to meet burner height and importantly, it was not made for moving the trolley with load which was the lapse committed by the petitioner.

Further the forklifts are always available in the foundry department for moving the treatment ladle and there will not be any issues of non availability/shortage of forklift and the petitioner without informing his supervisor to move the trolley by hand although he ought to have waited for the forklift to move the ladle.
The accident happened despite the respondent having provided safety equipment and followed the safety procedures.
This accident has occurred purely on account of the petitioner not exercising caution.
12. The respondent has contended that they continued to bear the cost of all of the treatment given to the petitioner and he has also been retained in the respondent's employment.
The respondent also did not reduce the salary or emoluments of the petitioner, despite his disability.

13. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves
that on the date of alleged incident i.e., on 16-02- 2022 in the first shift 6-00 am., to 2-00 pm., he is a workman employed in the respondent Factory ?

2) Whether the petitioner proves he suffered injuries during the course of employment or injury relates to the employment?
3) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so how much and from whom?

14.
In order to prove the case, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and two witnesses as Pw.2 and Pw.3 and got marked documents as per Ex.P1 to P20.

The respondent has examined its official as RW1 and got marked documents as per Ex.R1 to Ex.R7.
15.
Heard the arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and learned counsel for respondent 16.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final Order,
 for the following:-
 REASONS 17.

Issue No.1: So far as the relationship of employer and employee between the petitioner and respondent is concerned, the respondent nowhere has disputed the fact of petitioner working in the respondent company.

In the written statement, at para no. 5.12, the respondent has admitted that petitioner is a regular employee in the respondent Factory from 05-08-2009 and on 16-02-2022 ie.,
on the date of incident the petitioner was on duty in 'A' shift ( 6-00 am., to 2-00 pm.,).
Hence, when respondent has admitted the Employer and Employee relationship, further more discussion is not required on the issue no.1.
Hence, issue no.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
18. ISSUE NO.2 :
It is the contention taken by the petitioner that he has suffered injuries during the course of employment, hence respondent is liable to pay the compensation.

19. The respondent while admitting that petitioner is their employee and on 16-02-2022 he was working in their factory, has denied the injuries sustained by the petitioner during the course of employment.

It was vehemently argued by the learned counsel for respondent that the accident in question did not arise out of and in the course of his employment for the reason that the accident in question has occurred because the petitioner without authorization or instruction entered the ladle preheating area and willfully disobeyed safety protocols by manually moving 350 kg treatment ladle which resulted in the toppling of the trolley with the ladle on his right ankle causing the accident.

It was further submitted that the petitioner was exclusively assigned to the pouring activity and was strictly prohibited from engaging in the ladle preheating activity as per the Standard Operating Procedures.

The activity of ladle preheating was assigned to two other employees of the respondent on the date of the accident who would have as per SOP taken the assistance of the forklift operators to move the trolley with the ladle and that pouring activity assigned to the petitioner does not require him to be present in the ladle preheating activity area which is altogether a different and distinct process governed by its own SOP.
The Learned counsel in further has submitted that the petitioner had received extensive and repeated safety training initially in respect of both the ladle Pre-Heating activity and pouring activity.

In order to evidence the said fact the respondent has Kiran K R vs Fedaral Mogul Goetze India Ltd on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115107610/
4 produced "On Job Training Report" along with the "Participant Reaction Sheets" as per Ex.R5,
Ex.R6 and Ex.R7.

entities.text: Kiran K R vs Fedaral Mogul Goetze India Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If the said documents are perused, it bears the signature of petitioner.

The petitioner in his evidence has admitted the training given to him on safety measures and equipment planning and also admitted that after the completion of training, it will be reported in "On Job Training Report".
It is true that PW.1 in his cross examination has admitted that he is aware of the danger in moving the trolley manually and that a specific policy for using forklifts for this purpose was in place.
Regarding generating the feed back and reaction sheets in respect of the training is concerned, PW.1 has pleaded ignorance.

As observed supra, from the Ex.R5, Ex.R6 and Ex.R7 it can be gathered that after receiving the training "On Job Training Reports" along with "Participant Reaction Sheets"
have to be generated.
20. The learned counsel for respondent has vehemently submitted that at the time of accident the forklift operators were present on site performing tasks assigned to them.

If the cross examination of PW.1 is perused, PW.1 has admitted that the forklifts and trolleys are there in their factory and there is separate company policies in that regard and that on the date of accident forklifts operators were in the company but they were working in different places ie., they were working in the store room.
It is admitted by PW.1 that as per the company rules forklifts operators are there in their company.

21. The learned counsel for respondent has vehemently submitted that in order to claim compensation u/Sec. 3 of the ECA, the petitioner has to prove that accident arose both "out of" and "in the course of" his employment.

The Learned counsel at this juncture has referred the judgment reported in AIR 1970 SC 1906 between Mackinon Mackenzie and Co. (P) Ltd., Vs. Ibrahim Mahmmed Issak, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court has clarified the terms "in the course of employment" and "arising out of employment" .

entities.text: Mackinon Mackenzie and Co. (P) Ltd., Vs. Ibrahim Mahmmed Issak
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has affirmed the doctrine of "Added Peril", which stipulates that an employer is not liable if any employee, by their own imprudent act, exposes themselves to a risk that is not incidental to their employment.

The Court cited with approval the test laid down in Lancashire and Yorkshire Railway Company Vs. Highley: "Was it part of the Injured person's employment to hazard, to suffer, or to do that which caused his Injury?

entities.text: Lancashire and Yorkshire Railway Company Vs. Highley:
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If yes, the accident arose out of his employment.
In nay, it did not.... ".

It also added "To put it differently, if the accident had occurred on account of a risk which is an incident of the employment, the claim for compensation must succeed, unless of course the workman has exposed himself to an added peril by his own imprudent act".
22.

By referring the observation made in the aforesaid judgment it is vehemently argued by the Learned counsel for respondent that the Act of the petitioner was an instance of "Added Peril" and the work done by the petitioner on the stated date, at the stated place was outside the scope of employment as petitioner of his own exposed himself to a risk that is not incidental to his employment as admittedly petitioner's role on the said date was in the pouring activity as evident from production report at Ex.R3 and the accident occurred when the petitioner ventured in to the "preheating activity" area and engaged with a treatment ladle, a task governed by a separate SOP as per Ex.R2 and assigned to other employees.

sentences.text: The RW.1 in his evidence has deposed that petitioner was never instructed to involve himself in the "preheating process" and two other employees namely Mr. Sriram and Mr. S Manjunath were assigned with that job and petitioner had no instructions to perform it.
24. Now at this juncture it would be relevant to refer here the evidence of PW.1.

The PW.1 in his petition and evidence has categorically stated that though he was designated with the work of "pouring activities" but on the said date he received instruction from his supervisor Narasimhamurthy through fixed term employee Mr. Ravikumar to place the pouring ladle to Burner-1, preheating in order to start pouring.
At that time he observed that the treatment ladle was already placed for preheating and Burner-1 by his co-workers Prabhulingh and M Sriram.
Further he observed that the treatment ladle heating had been completed and the burner was in AUTOOFF condition.

As no other workers or forklift was available in preheating area as forklift operators were engaged in the working of stocking charging materials next to the furnace, as per the instructions of the supervisor to place the pouring ladle for preheating to start pouring through fixed term employee, he attempted to pull the trolley backside manually on which 350 kg treatment ladle was placed for preheating at Burner-1.
In that process he sustained injuries.

25. It was vehemently argued by the learned counsel for respondent that except the bald statement of the petitioner that he was instructed by supervisor Narsimha Murthy to do the pouring activities through fixed term employee Mr. Ravi Kumar, he has not taken any steps to examine them as witness, hence the assertion made by the petitioner remained unsubstantiated and they are nothing more than an after thoughts devise to mask the petitioner's negligence and to make a wrongful claim against the respondent.

It was further argued that when the petitioner knew the consequences of moving 350 kg trolleys manually and when forklift operators were available in the site, the decision of the petitioner to pull a trolley unilaterally and manually is contrary to the established procedure and his training and the said act of the petitioner is nothing but will full act of disobedience and disregard for safety procedure and it was not part of his duty, hence accident did not arise out of employment.
Hence, respondent is statutorily except from liability.

26. In the light of the argument canvassed by the learned counsel for respondent, if the documents placed on record is perused, it is not in dispute that on the date of accident, petitioner was deputed to do pouring activity.
It is also not in dispute that at the relevant time of accident he was working in preheating Area.
It is also not in dispute that the petitioner while doing work in Preheating Area sustained injuries.
Admittedly the petitioner was given training in both the areas.
The very fact of training given in both the area discloses that in an emergency the workers who have gained training in both the areas have to work in both the areas.
It is not the case of the respondent that petitioner having no training in preheating area and without gaining any knowledge in preheating area ventured to do the said activities.

In the present case, as per the case of petitioner, he was directed by supervisor Narasimha Murthy through co-worker Ravi Kumar to do work in Preheating Area to place the pouring ladle to Burnder 1 for pre-heating.
It is true that petitioner has not examined either Narasimha Murthy or Ravi Kumar to substantiate the said fact.

But it is relevant to state here that with regard to the accident, case of negligence was registered by the Deputy Director for Factories Division -3 in CC No.15175 of 2022 u/Sec. 92 of the Factories Act.

The said case was registered against Rajesh Sinha the occupier and Sri Girish Prabhu the factory Manager of the Kiran K R vs Fedaral Mogul Goetze India Ltd on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115107610/
6 respondent company.

entities.text: Kiran K R vs Fedaral Mogul Goetze India Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case the accused had admitted their guilty and deposited the fine amount.

It was vehemently argued by the learned counsel for respondent that the proceedings under the Factories Act are penal in nature focusing on regulatory compliance, while proceedings under the ECA are civil determining entitlement.
A guilty plea in a criminal matter often made to avoid protracted litigation which does not absolve the petitioner of his burden to prove his case on a preponderance of probabilities.
The plea is not an admission that the petitioner's actions were justified or that accident arose out of employment.
It was further argued that the petitioner failed to discharge the burden of proof to establish that the alleged incident arose out of and in the course of employment.
The learned counsel by referring Mackinnon Mackenzie case has submitted that the court cannot base its findings on Surmise, conjecture or guess, it must draw legitimate inference from proved facts.
27. If the complaint filed u/Sec. 200 Cr.PC under the Factories Act as per Ex.P1 is perused, it discloses that after the accident internal investigation was done.
RW.1 has deposed that he was the part of the said internal investigation team.
After receiving information about the accident, the Deputy Director of Factories conducted enquiry and investigation.
A report was issued covering the details of enquires conducted.
During the course of enquiry/investigation Sri Prabhulinga, M Sriram and M Ravikumar have given statement and their statement was recorded.
On such enquiry and inspection it was revealed that Trolleys used in the factory for movement of treatment ladles have not been engineered for safe movement at all time.
Unevenness and level differences in flooring caused the toppling of the trolley resulting in the accident in subject.

Though SOP were prepared and in the place for preheating of ladles, but some time workers not able to carry out the preheating of ladles as per SOP due to non availability of forklift or co-workers is not a sound engineering practice.

On such investigation/Enquiry it was concluded that there was lack of supervision and had there was a strict supervision from competent person, petitioner would not have ventured to pull back the trolley in unsafe condition and held that there was a positive omission on the part of the respondent.
28. Now at this juncture it would be relevant to refer here the cross examination of RW.1.
Admittedly RW.1 is not an eye witness to the accident.

It is the evidence of RW.1 that he is one of the member in the Investigation Team and Ravi Prasad safety officer, Vidhya Sagar, Shift Engineer Narasimha Murthy, Maintenance Manager Balaji, Ajay Baradwaj and plant Manager Girish Prabhu were also there in the said investigation team.

29. If the Ex.P1 is perused, wherein there is reference about the statement given by Sri Prabhulinga,
M Sriram and M Ravi Kumar on 08-04-2022 regarding the accident.

Even though respondent has disputed the negligence on their part and bent upon contended that on the date of accident petitioner was entrusted with the pouring activity and not the preheating activity of treatment ladle and that he was supposed to restrict himself to the SOP related to the pouring activity and thereby himself caused for the accident but the respondent for the reason best known to them have not produced the investigation report which contains the statement of the aforesaid persons.
Further the RW.1 being part of the investigation team and the Ex.P1 was lodged on the basis of the said investigation team cannot dispute the correctness of the complaint lodged under Ex.P1.

It is true that the judgment given in Criminal Case is not binding on the Tribunal and the Tribunal has to Kiran K R vs Fedaral Mogul Goetze India Ltd on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115107610/
7 independently decide the case but in the present case if really the respondent had dispute the allegation against made in the Ex.P1, they could have contest the case registered against them under Factories Act as per ExP1.

entities.text: Kiran K R vs Fedaral Mogul Goetze India Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The accused person arrayed in the Ex.P1 are the responsible official of the respondent Factory.

If really the accident in question was not occurred due to the negligence of the respondent and if really the petitioner was not entrusted with the work of preheating activity,
definitely the respondent could have contested the case registered under Ex.P1.
There is no reason assigned why they have admitted the guilty in the Criminal Case registered against them under Ex.P1.

If really the petitioner was not entrusted with preheating activity by Narasimha Murthy, in order to substantiate the defence, the respondent could have examined Narasimha Murthy and Ravi Kumar as their witness.

The Learned counsel for respondent has submitted that it is for the petitioner to examine Narasimha Murthy and Ravi Kumar as witness to prove that on the date of accident Mr. Narasimha Murthy through Ravi Kumar has entrusted the work of preheating activity.

But this court is of the opinion that when petitioner has produced Ex.P1 and admittedly the accused in Ex.P1 have admitted their guilty and deposited fine amount and when there is reference in the Ex.P1 about the statement given by the officials of respondent aforementioned and when the respondent has not produced the said statements, under such circumstances in order to negative the claim of the petitioner, the respondent could have examined the supervisor Narasimha Murthy as witness.
30.
It is not in dispute that petitioner has incurred medical expenses to the tune of nearly Rs.22,44,240/- and the entire medical expenses was met by the respondent.

If really, accident in question was occurred not due to the negligence on the part of the respondent the question of meeting the medical expenses would not arise and it would not necessitated the respondent to meet the medical expenses of the petitioner.
The learned counsel for respondent submitted that out of humanitarian ground they have met the medical expenses of the petitioner.
But this court is not accepting the said version of the respondent for the reason that sum of Rs.22,44,240/- is not a meager amount so as to meet the said expenses on humanitarian ground.
If really the accident in question has not occurred due to the negligence of the respondent definitely respondent would not have ventured to meet the medical expenses.

31. Hence, the very fact that petitioner was given training in both the activities ie., pouring activities and preheating activities, the very fact that the respondent has not produced investigation report and has not examined Narasimha Murthy and Ravi Kumar as witness and the very fact that the entire medical expenses was borne out by the respondent and the fact that accused persons in CC No.15175/2022 had admitted their guilty by admitting the entire negligence contributed by the respondent and the very admitted fact that petitioner was the employee of the respondent and the accident in question has occurred while he was discharging his duties in the Factory, under such circumstances it can be said without any hesitation that the accident in question was due to the negligence on the part of the respondent and it cannot be said that the petitioner by his own imprudent act exposes himself to a risk that is not incidental to his work.
The work done by the petitioner was not outside the scope of his employment.
Hence, it can be said that the accident in question has occurred out of and in the course of employment.

sentences.text: Now at this juncture it would be relevant to refer here the judgment of hon'ble Supreme court rendered in Jaya Biswal' and Others / Branch Manager IFFCO TOKIO GENEGAL INSUANCE COMPANY LIMITED AND OTHERS reported in 2016)11 SCC 201 where in while distinguishing the claim under MV Act as well as the Employees Compensation Act held that negligence on the part of the claimant cannot be considered and compensation cannot be reduced for contributory negligence.

entities.text: IFFCO TOKIO GENEGAL INSUANCE COMPANY LIMITED AND OTHERS reported in 2016)11 SCC 201
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 33. Further in MFA No.1936/2017 dated 24/7/2019 the hon'ble High Court while discussing about the claim made under MV Act as well as E.C Act held that negligence on the part of the workmen attracts only under the provisions of the Motor vehicles Act and the said provision has no bearing on the facts of the case in EC Act.
The provisions of the E.C Act do not envisage a situation where the compensation payable to an injured or deceased workmen can be reduced on account of contributory negligence.
In view of the discussion made herein above, this court answers issue no.2 in the Affirmative.
34. Issue No.3: In view of the discussion made herein above the petitioner has proved the employee and employer relationship so also the injuries sustained during the course of employment.
35. The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents which are at Ex.P3, Ex.P7 and Ex.P8.

On going through the medical documents it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment at Manipal Hospitals,
Bangalore for two times ie., from 16-02-2022 to 21-02-2022 and from 03-01-2024 to 06- 01-2024.
The petitioner has taken treatment for a period of 10 days.
The petitioner has sustained right ankle and foot crush injury with heavy object.

As per the Disability Certificate, the petitioner has sustained right Ankle and Crush injury by Open reduction and Internal fixation of Talus bone and Medial Malleolus with rightankle reconstruction, Multiple Fracture Fixation, Tendon repair Debridement and Nerve Decompression was done.

The petitioner has sustained permanent disability of 45% to the right leg (Locomotor & Physical disability) .
36.

Dr. R Shashikanth, Medical Officer/Assistant Surgeon at Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru is examined as PW.2, through him Inpatient record, MLC register, Police Intimation, x-ray film and Disability Assessment report are got marked as Ex.P12 to Ex.P16.
As per the evidence of PW.2, he examined the petitioner on 17-04-2024 for assessment of disability.
His disability was assessed on clinical examination (mobility component, stability component and additional fractures).
The petitioner has 45% disability for right ankle.
37. PW.2 further deposed that he examined the petitioner again on 30-06-2025 for further treatment and assessment of disability.
The petitioner came limping with the help of a metallic crutches as support.
The petitioner complains of pain in the right ankle and foot burning sensation in the right leg and right knee.

He has difficulty in standing for long time, running, walking for a distance, climbing stairs, squatting and using Indian toilets he has difficulty in driving two wheeler with gear and work in the Factory like before.

sentences.text: PW.2 further deposed that petitioner has sustained permanent disability of 45% on the right leg and 15% on the whole body.
39. If the cross examination of PW.2 is perused, PW.2 was in the medical team who had given treatment to the petitioner and conducted surgery.

From the evidence of PW.2 it can be gathered that earlier to the disability assessed by the Pw.2, the disability of petitioner was assessed by the Government Hospital wherein also the disability on right leg was assessed at 45%.
The respondent has not denied the said fact.

40. The petitioner has examined Dr. Naveen S Shetty -Specialist, Orthopedic Surgeon at KC General Hospital, Bangalore as PW.3 and got marked x-ray film, OPD register along with bill, Assessment Proforma, Disability certificate are got marked at Ex.P.17 to P20.
41.
As this court had recorded the statement of petitioner, court had the opportunity to see the petitioner.
In almost all the hearing dates the petitioner used to appear before the court.
The petitioner is using walking stick in support and even now also he is not completely recovered from the injuries.
42. Under such circumstances this court inclines to take the disability as 15% on whole body which is the disability assessed by the PW.2 on whole body of the petitioner.
43. Petitioner has contended that he was aged about 42 years as on the date of accident.
In order to prove his age proof, the petitioner has produced Aadhar card, wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 13-06- 1983.
The accident in question has occurred on 16-02- 2022.
Hence the age of petitioner is taken as 39 years.
44. The petitioner in his petition has contended that, he was employee under the Respondent and earning Rs.50,000/- per month
The petitioner has produced salary slip as per Ex.P9.

As per Ex.P9,
the gross salary of petitioner was Rs.58,937/- and net salary was Rs.33,966/-.
45.
It is well settled that when there is no evidence to prove the income of the petitioner, court has to rely upon the minimum wages provided under Employees compensation Act.

In the Gazette of India Notification New Delhi dated 3rd Jan 2020 wherein, exercise of the powers conferred by sub section (1B) of section 4 of the Employees Compensation Act 1923 (8 of 1923) and in supersession of the notification of the Ministry of Labour and Employment issued vide number S.O 1258 (E) dated 31st May 2010 published in the Gazette of India Specified for the purpose of sub section (1) of the said section, sum of Rs.15,000/- as monthly wages with effect from the date of publication of notification in the official gazette.
